title: Chemical Bonding: Ionic and Covalent
text: Chemical bonds hold atoms together in compounds. Ionic bonds form when one atom transfers electrons to another, creating oppositely charged ions that attract each other (e.g., sodium chloride, table salt). Covalent bonds form when atoms share electron pairs (e.g., water, H2O). Metallic bonds involve a shared sea of electrons among metal atoms, explaining conductivity and malleability. Bond type strongly influences a compound's melting point, solubility, and electrical conductivity.
